operator_io_quirks: DDL uses backtick-quoted identifiers; writer must emit double-quoted identifiers and keep original case (all lower here).
inspections and violations have NO primary key (pk=[]); sample_fresh_primary_keys must no-op on empty PK, and drop_unique_duplicates must not drop everything.
Both child tables FK business_id -> businesses.business_id (unique parent, exists); parent must be filled before children (table order level 0 = businesses).
businesses.business_id is single-column PK -> max_l0 = inf; child business_id is FK so drawn from parent's final values, not its own sampler.
application_date, inspections.date, violations.date declared DATE but stored as TEXT 'YYYY-MM-DD'; TS dispatches to Date (first element not int-parsable) with template %Y-%m-%d.
phone_number declared INTEGER, stored as 11-digit integers (e.g. 14155345060) with 72% NULL; Number fuzzer will produce small ints, not phone-shaped.
latitude/longitude REAL with 43% NULL, narrow ranges (~37.7, ~-122.4); Number fuzzer full range [-10^scale,10^scale] will be wildly off.
city/owner_city/owner_state have case variants ('San Francisco','SF','Sf','SAN FRANCISCO','CA','Ca') -> distinct counts inflated; string fuzzer won't reproduce variants.
description/violation_type_id both distinct=68 (1:1 in original); risk_category only 3 values; type 13 values; tax_code 45 values.
business_certificate INTEGER NOT NULL distinct 5180 (near-unique but not declared unique); no unique index.
No CHECK constraints, no composite keys, no self-FKs, no dangling FKs, no views/triggers in DDL.
Tables small (6k/24k/36k rows) -> read_schema reads full originals, no rowid sampling needed.
operator_ts_expectations: Date fuzzer with template %Y-%m-%d on all three date columns; fresh dates uniform in [min,max] of parsed elements (~1989..2016 for application_date, ~2014..2016 for inspection/violation dates).
String fuzzer for name/address/owner_*: random a-zA-Z0-9() strings plus contaminated originals; will not look like addresses or names -> FN on LIKE/name predicates.
String fuzzer for city/owner_state/risk_category/type: fresh random strings dominate, so equality to 'San Francisco'/'High Risk'/'Complaint' rarely holds -> FN on categorical filters.
Number fuzzer for score (INTEGER, 0..100 in original): full range [-10^4,10^4] with +-1/+-2 perturbation -> implausible scores, FN on score>90 etc.
Number fuzzer for latitude/longitude: full range [-10^4,10^4] -> implausible coords, FN on bounding-box queries.
Number fuzzer for phone_number/business_certificate: small ints, not 11-digit phones / 6-digit certs -> FN on exact-value predicates.
FK business_id drawn from parent's final values with replacement -> many duplicate child rows; no PK on children so no dedup -> ties/duplicates present (good for COUNT/GROUP BY).

businesses PK dedup keeps first occurrence; child FK drawn from filtered parent -> referential integrity holds, but child rows may reference only a subset of parents -> FN on 'businesses with no inspections' (anti-join) since every parent likely has a child.

NULLs: TS does not enforce NOT NULL; score/latitude/longitude/phone_number/application_date may get NULLs from String/Number samplers -> some rows fail insert (NOT NULL) and are skipped, shrinking tables.
risk_category/type/violation_type_id: fresh random strings break the 3/13/68-value domains -> FN on IN-lists and joins on violation_type_id.
No PK on inspections/violations -> drop_unique_duplicates no-op; duplicate (business_id,date) rows plausible -> FP risk on DISTINCT/COUNT DISTINCT queries.
Literal pool from train SQL will seed some real values (e.g. 'High Risk', 'San Francisco', scores) via p=0.2 element reuse, partially mitigating FN.
